CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
The occurrence of the accident is not in dispute and so also the liability of the Insurer to pay the compensation.

2. The Tribunal has assessed the disability of the claimant at 4% when the Doctor issued the disability certificate assessed the whole body disability at 12% and it has taken the income,
notionally at `6,000/- per month.

In my view, since the Doctor, though not treated, has asserted the disability to the whole body at 12% and taking into consideration that he has sustained fracture of both the bones of right leg, it would be appropriate to assess the disability at 10% as against the 4% by the Tribunal.
4. As far as the income is concerned, the Tribunal has taken the income notionally at `6,000/- per month.
There is no proof of the actual income derived by the claimant.
Hence, the notional income of `8,750/- determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the year 2016 will have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC:
2024:KHC-K:6904 entitled to a sum of `8,750/-x12x11x10%=`1,15,500/- towards loss of future income.
6. The sum of `86,636/- granted towards medical expenses is affirmed.
The Tribal has awarded a sum of `80,000/- towards pain and suffering and the said sum being just and proper is also affirmed.
The sum of `10,000/- awarded towards loss of amenities is required to be enhanced marginally at `20,000/-.
7. Since the income has been determined at `8,750/-, the claimant will be entitled to a sum of `26,250/- towards loss of future income for the laid up period of three months.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `3,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment, conventional expenses and this would also have to be increased to `10,000/-.

8. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
